A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Empirical Privacy Variance by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2/Enron and Llama-2/TOFU experiments, hyperparameter regressions, heuristic evaluations, and privacy-auditing results in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds maximum-over-secrets privacy-score analyses in Appendix F, including new regressions and correlations.

M1.justification: The hyperparameter-selection procedure in Algorithm 1 and the DP-SGD/DP-Adam algorithms remain unchanged. The maximum-score analysis changes evaluation aggregation, not the proposed training or selection procedure. Shuffled sampling was already disclosed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use Enron and the same TOFU variants, secret sets, and fine-tuning tasks. Appendix F analyzes existing Enron coverage under another score aggregation. Diffusion models remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: The best-utility and worst-utility selection baselines, oracle reference, and random-guess comparator remain unchanged in their respective experiments. The RDP, PRV, and Connect-the-Dots accountant comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds evaluation using the maximum per-secret score instead of the mean, applying it to variance plots, regression responses, and auditing correlations. This supplements the original evaluation; existing splits, model configurations, training budgets, and mean-score analyses are retained.

E4.justification: The new Appendix F tests whether averaging over secrets explains the findings. Figure 30 checks privacy variance under maximum aggregation, Table 13 checks hyperparameter trends, and additional correlations check auditing alignment. This is a focused robustness extension to the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Training-seed counts in Table 6, three ACR search seeds in Appendix B.7, 5,000 Monte Carlo trials in Appendix D.3, and regression significance-reporting practices are retained. The new regressions use the existing reporting practice; no additional uncertainty procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: Appendix F adds maximum-score results: Table 13 reports individual-hyperparameter coefficients of 0.38, 1.31, and 1.80, while auditing correlation is -0.29 and mean-versus-maximum correlation is 0.90. These supplement unchanged mean-score results under a different metric. Table 2 also corrects the TOFU batch-size significance marker from two to three stars, retaining p = 2 × 10^-5.

T1.justification: Appendix F introduces a limited definitional extension: an empirical-privacy score taking the maximum over secrets instead of their average. The DP definition, per-secret metric definitions, and existing mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same claims about privacy variance, hyperparameter trade-offs, selection heuristics, and unresolved explanations. The shortened conclusion preserves the central claim, while the added robustness evidence supports the existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly interprets the maximum-score results as evidence of a gap between DP's protection and memorization-based privacy measures. It expands the existing sampler caveat to discuss underestimated privacy loss and justify retaining shuffled batches. It also adds discussion of GDP and full-profile reporting, including their potential limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly announces public project code and supplies its repository link in Section 3.1 and Appendix B. Existing implementation settings and hardware/runtime disclosures are retained; the compute appendix moves from F to G rather than being newly added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gomez et al. (2025) on DP reporting, Staab et al. (2024) on inference risks, and Ho et al. (2020) and Song et al. (2021) on diffusion models. It removes the Carlini et al. diffusion-extraction citation. The central positioning relative to Hayes et al. and Kaissis et al. remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the combined conclusion/future-directions section with an expanded discussion and a separate short conclusion, lightly rewrites related work, and inserts Appendix F. Most of the main narrative and existing appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: New Figure 30 pairs the retained average-score plot with maximum-score results, and new Table 13 compares their regressions. Earlier figures are retained. Runtime and complete-results displays are renumbered and relocated, with local appendix reflow but no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The new Appendix F strengthens evidence that the findings are not simply artifacts of averaging over secrets, and the code-access statement improves reproducibility information. These are focused gains. The maximum over curated secrets remains narrower than DP's formal worst-case quantification, so Section 7's stronger interpretation is not fully established; the acknowledged sampler/accountant mismatch also remains unresolved.
